🇺🇦 Kiev regional council deputies caught funneling poverty-assistance funds to their own families

Deputies of the Kiev regional council allocated money meant for the poor to their own families instead. Nine people are now under suspicion — the deputies themselves and their close relatives — according to Ukraine's National Police.

The funds were siphoned through the regional social program "Zabota" ("Care"), designed for those in genuine need of social assistance.

Law enforcement says the deputies' relatives and trusted associates received payments — in some cases reaching hundreds of thousands of hryvnia.

In one case, the parents of one suspect repeatedly received "medical treatment" assistance between 2021 and 2025, despite police finding they were not in financial hardship. The deputy's mother acquired real estate and an expensive car during this period worth a combined 3.5 million+ hryvnia.

Some of the funds are alleged to have gone toward cosmetic procedures and other personal services.

Police estimate the total damage at over 3 million hryvnia.

💬 Iran ranks among world’s top five in power plant technology: Energy minister

📌 Bojnurd, IRNA – Iran ranks among the world’s top five countries in power plant technology, with a significant share of domestically manufactured power equipment exported to international markets, Energy Minister Abbas Aliabadi has said.

Speaking at the inauguration of the 72-megawatt Esfarayen power plant in North Khorasan Province on Thursday, Aliabadi said Iran has achieved a prominent position in power generation technology and exports much of its locally produced equipment to various countries.
​
He said Iran is entering a new era and has emerged as a global power, adding that the administration of President Masoud Pezeshkian is working to serve the public.
​
The future belongs to energy, Aliabadi said, stressing the need to pursue electricity industry development seriously.
​
The minister also highlighted progress in renewable energy, saying Iran has launched a sustainable drive toward developing new energy sources and has prioritized investment in solar power plants.
​
He emphasized, however, that increasing generation capacity must be accompanied by advances in technology.
​
Aliabadi said Iran holds a strong position in electricity industry investment and noted that the country’s pace of development in the sector remains significant.
